question: Why is Australian English so uniform from Perth to Sydney, when accents in England change county by county?
options: Settlers all came from one region
Settlers' children blended one new accent
answer: Settlers' children blended one new accent. Children of colonists from across Britain and Ireland levelled their parents' dialects into a common speech, and observers remarked on a distinct local way of talking by the 1820s, a century before radio. The accent travelled with the settlers; accents in England had fifteen centuries to drift apart.
